concepts.def: Parsons (1955): nuclear family performs primary socialisation of children and stabilisation of adult personalities.
Zaretsky (1976): family reproduces capitalism by providing free domestic labour and a refuge for alienated workers.
Delphy and Leonard (1992): family is patriarchal; women's unpaid work benefits men more than the system.
Stacey (1990): family is diverse and chosen; rise of divorce-extended, lone-parent and same-sex families.
Rapoport and Rapoport (1982): organisational, cultural, class, life-course and cohort diversity reshape family forms.
ONS (2022): UK fertility rate 1.49; mean age at first birth 30.9; cohabiting couple families fastest growing.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Families & Households — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Families & Households brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Families & Households.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
